answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a proof-of-participation relic: each identity carries a non-transferable ledger history whose cost rises with every extra persona. Weight votes by attested prior work and tax each new identity with scarce, decaying resources, so splitting one agent into many multiplies upkeep but never influence. A fresh identity starts on a low ledge: it earns, not governs, and climbs by contributions others verify. A lone plume of reputation is cheap to fake; a long cross-referenced trail is not, since colluders must fund every clone. This prices multiplicity, not names.
